parole.testo: From the genus name, translingual Abelmoschus.
Most likely derived from translingual Australopithecus.
Borrowed from translingual Amorpha, from Ancient Greek ἄμορφος (ámorphos, “shapeless”).

parole.significato: Any tick of the genus Argas.
ascomycete, a fungus of the taxon Ascomycota.
Any mushroom of the genus Auriscalpium.
A scarab beetle of the genus Aphodius.
mosquito orchid; any plant of the genus Acianthus.

parole.testo: From translingual Bombycina, from translingual Bombyx.
Calque of translingual Solenogastres. From боро́здка (borózdka, “groove”) + брю́хо (brjúxo, “belly”) + -ий (-ij, adjectival suffix).

parole.significato: Any plant in the genus Brachylaena.
Any moss of the genus Bryoerythrophyllum.
a krait; a venomous elapid snake of the genus Bungarus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Bungarus m, itself from Telugu బంగారు (baṅgāru, “golden”, adjective).

parole.significato: Any snake of the genus Atractus.
parole.testo: веретенови́дный (veretenovídnyj, “spindle-shaped”) + змея́ (zmejá, “snake”), a calque of translingual Atractus.
By surface analysis, водоро́д (vodoród, “hydrogen”) + -ка (-ka, diminutive suffix). Likely a calque of translingual Hydraena.
вода́ (vodá, “water”) + -о- (-o-) + краса́ (krasá, “beauty”), a calque of translingual Hydrocharis.
Calque of translingual Aquilegia, вода́ (vodá) + -о- (-o-) + сбор (sbor).
Calque of translingual Lycodon, as волк (volk, “wolf”) + зуб (zub, “tooth”).
Borrowed from translingual Volvox, from Latin volvō (“to roll”).

parole.significato: Any mushroom of the genus Galerina.

parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Heliamphora. From a compound of Ancient Greek ἥλῐος m (hḗlĭos, “sun”) + Latin amphora f (“amphora”).

parole.significato: Any extinct bird of the genus Hesperornis.
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Hesperornis, from Ancient Greek ἕσπερος (hésperos, “western”) + Ancient Greek ὄρνις (órnis, “bird”).

parole.significato: Any fungus of the genus Hydenellum.
Any ladybug of the genus Hippodamia.
Any mushroom of the genus Hypholoma.

parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Gladiolus, from Latin gladiolus (“little sword, sword lily”), diminutive of gladius (“sword”).

parole.significato: nudibranchian, belonging to or characteristic of the Nudibranchia or nudibranchs.
parole.testo: From го́лый (gólyj, “nude, naked”) + -о- (-o-, vocalic interfix) + жа́бра (žábra, “gill(s)”) + -ный (-nyj, adjectival suffix), literally “naked-gilled”, a calque of translingual Nudibranchia, (from nūdus (“naked, nude”) + branchia (“gill(s)”)).

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Goniolimon.

parole.testo: горо́шек (goróšek, “vetch”) + мохна́тый (moxnátyj, “hairy”), a calque of translingual Vicia villosa.

parole.significato: Davallia canariensis, a species of fern from Macaronesia and Iberia.
parole.testo: дава́ллия (davállija, “Davallia”) + кана́рский (kanárskij, “Canarian, relating to the Canary Islands”), a calque of translingual Davallia canariensis.
Borrowed from translingual Dinosauria, from Ancient Greek δεινός (deinós, “scary, awful”) + σαῦρος (saûros, “lizard”).

parole.significato: Any fern in the genus Diplazium.
Any snake of the genus Dolichophis.
A longhorn beetle of the genus Macrodontia, noted for their large proportions and the males' mandibles.
parole.testo: The term is a calque of translingual Macrodontia (literally “large-toothed”), from дровосе́к (drovosék, “lumberjack, longhorn beetle”) + большезу́б (bolʹšezúb, “bigtooth”, noun, respective adjective большезу́бый (bolʹšezúbyj)).
From ель f (jelʹ, “spruce; fir”) + Шре́нка (Šrénka, “of Schrenk”, genitive proper noun), a calque of translingual Picea schrenkiana.
жи́молость (žímolostʹ, “honeysuckle”) + монетоли́стный (monetolístnyj, “coin-leaved”), calque of translingual Lonicera nummulariifolia.
From жиро́ндский (žiróndskij, “of Gironde”) + медя́нка (medjánka, “grass snake”), a calque of translingual Coronella girondica.
From змея́ (zmejá, “snake”) + голова́ (golová, “head”) + -ник (-nik), a calque of translingual Dracocephalum.

parole.significato: Any mushroom of the genus Inonotus.

parole.testo: и́рис (íris, “iris”) + герма́нский (germánskij, “German”), literally “German iris”, calque of translingual Iris × germanica.
и́рис (íris, “iris”) + ибери́йский (iberíjskij, “Iberian”), a calque of translingual Iris iberica.
и́рис (íris, “iris”) + тигро́вый (tigróvyj, “tiger”, relational adjective), a calque of translingual Iris tigridia.

parole.significato: Any asteraceous plant of the genus Cancrinia; a cancrinia.
caudofoveate, a mollusc of the class Caudofoveata.
Any fungus of the genus Clavulinopsis.
Any beetle of the genus Dermestes.
parole.testo: ко́жа (kóža, “skin”) + -ед (-ed, “eater”), a calque of translingual Dermestes.
From коза́ (kozá, “goat”) + -о- (-o-) + дои́ть (doítʹ, “to milk”), a calque of translingual Caprimulgus.

parole.significato: Any casebearer moth of the genus Coleophora.

parole.testo: коловра́т (kolovrát, “whirl, swirl”) + -ка (-ka), a calque of translingual Rotifera.

parole.significato: Any snake of the genus Kolpophis, the only species sometimes considered valid being Kolpophis annandalei (syn. Hydrophi…

parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Combretum, from Latin combrētum.

parole.significato: A caterpillar hunter, a beetle of the genus Calosoma.
parole.testo: крас(ивый) (kras(ivyj), “beautiful”) + -о- (-o-) + тел(о) (tel(o), “body”); calque of translingual Calosoma.
Borrowed from translingual Krascheninnikovia, itself from Крашени́нников (Krašenínnikov, “Krasheninnikov”, surname).
Calque of translingual Cyrtodactylus, as кривопа́лый (krivopályj, “crooked-fingered”) + гекко́н (gekkón, “gecko”).

parole.significato: Any mushroom of the genus Crinipellis.
An ant of the genus Lasius.
A flat-faced longhorn beetle, a lamiine.

parole.testo: Neuter plural of линя́ющий (linjájuščij, “molting”), from линя́ть (linjátʹ, “to molt”). Calque of translingual Ecdysozoa.
From лук (luk, “onion”) + голубо́й (golubój, “sky-blue”), a calque of translingual Allium caeruleum.
Borrowed from translingual Macrolepiota. Surface analysis макро- (makro-, “macro-”) + лепио́та (lepióta, “Lepiota”).

parole.significato: Any green alga of the genus Microglena.
A myxophagan, any beetle of the suborder Myxophaga.

parole.testo: Calque of translingual Polydesmida, as много- (mnogo-, “multi-”) + связь (svjazʹ, “link, connection”) + -а (-a, nominal suffix). Compare многосвя́зный (mnogosvjáznyj).
мра́морный (mrámornyj, “marbled”) + краб (krab, “crab”), a partial calque of translingual Pachygrapsus marmoratus.

parole.significato: Any grass of the genus Muhlenbergia, a muhly.

parole.testo: Likely from the obsolete taxon of translingual Nemertini, now synonymous with the phylum Nemertea.

parole.significato: Any grass of the genus Neostapfia.

parole.testo: Calque of translingual Demospongiae, as обыкнове́нный (obyknovénnyj, “ordinary, normal”) + гу́бка (gúbka, “sponge”).
Calque of translingual Carex elongata, as осо́ка (osóka, “sedge”) + удлинённый (udlinjónnyj, “elongated”).
Borrowed from translingual Ochna, from Ancient Greek ὄχνη (ókhnē, “pear tree”).

parole.significato: Any lichen species of the genus Peltigera.

parole.testo: пло́ский (plóskij, “flat”) + че́рвь (čérvʹ, “worm”), literally “flat worm”, a calque of translingual Platyhelminthes.

parole.significato: A sea krait, a snake of the genus Laticauda.
parole.testo: пло́ский (plóskij, “flat”, adjective) + -о- (-o-) + хвост m (xvost, “tail”, noun), literally “flat-tail”. A calque of translingual Laticauda f, from Latin lātus (“wide, broad”, adjective) + Latin cauda f (“tail”), literally “broad-tail”.
Calque of translingual Hipposideridae, from the plural of подковогу́бый (podkovogúbyj), from подковогу́б (podkovogúb).
From пти́ца (ptíca, “bird”) + мле́ко (mléko, “milk”) + -ник (-nik), a calque of translingual Ornithogalum.
пупо́к (pupók, “belly button, navel”) + -ник (-nik), calque of translingual Omphalodes.
Calque of translingual Polyphaga, as разноя́дный (raznojádnyj, “polyphagous”) + жук (žuk, “beetle”).

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Rauvolfia.

parole.testo: рде́ст (rdést, “pondweed”) + гребе́нчатый (grebénčatyj, “pectinate”), A calque of translingual Stuckenia pectinata.
рого́з (rogóz, “Typha”) + узколи́стный (uzkolístnyj, “angustifolious”), a calque of translingual Typha angustifolia.
рододе́ндрон (rododéndron, “rhododendron”) + камча́тский (kamčátskij, “Kamchatkan”), a calque of translingual Rhododendron camtschaticum.
Partial calque of translingual Rhodomyrtus, building on Russian мирт (mirt, “myrtle”).
серде́чник (serdéčnik, “bittercress”) + лу́ковичный (lúkovičnyj, “bulbous”), a calque of translingual Cardamine bulbifera.

parole.significato: Any wasp of the genus Scolia.
Any skipper butterfly of the genus Spialia.
stylommatophorous; relating to the Stylommatophora order of gastropods.
parole.testo: Calque of translingual Stylommatophora, as стебелёк (stebeljók, “little stem, little stalk”) + глаз (glaz, “eye”) + -ый (-yj, adjectival suffix), literally “stalklet-eyed”.

parole.significato: stevia (a sweet herb and a sweetener)
Any beetle in the genus Scymnus.

parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual ternetzi (as the specific epithet of Gymnocorymbus ternetzi). The species was named after ichthyologist Carl Ternetz (whence also Anostomus ternetzi and Liotyphlops ternetzii). The surname originates from the Slavic languages. Compare Терниц (Ternic), likely related to Rus
тибе́тский (tibétskij, “Tibetan”) + во́рон (vóron, “raven”), a calque of translingual Corvus corax tibetanus.
то́поль (tópolʹ, “poplar”) + Фре́монт (Frémont, “Frémont”), a calque of translingual Populus fremontii.
Borrowed from translingual Trachymedusae and its singular form in New Latin trachymedusa. From New Latin trachy- (“spiky, jagged”, from Ancient Greek τρᾱχῠ́ς m (trākhŭ́s)) + New Latin medūsa f.

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Trichosanthes.
Any hide beetle of the genus Trox.
Tulipa lehmanniana, a species of tulip.
parole.testo: тюльпа́н (tjulʹpán, “tulip”) + Ле́ман (Léman, “Lehmann”), a calque of translingual Tulipa lehmanniana.
фиа́лка (fiálka, “violet (plant)”) + трёхцве́тный (trjoxcvétnyj, “tricolor, three-colored”), a calque of translingual Viola tricolor.
цика́да (cikáda, “cicada”) + -ка (-ka, diminutive suffix), a calque of translingual Cicadella, the type genus of the Cicadellidae.
From чешуя́ (češujá, “scales”) + крыло́ (kryló, “wing”) + -ый (-yj, adjectival suffix). Calque of translingual Lepidoptera.
Pluralization of Russian чешу́йчатый (češújčatyj, “scaly”), a semantic loan from translingual Squamata.

parole.significato: Austrian briar, Rosa foetida, a species of rose.
parole.testo: шипо́вник (šipóvnik, “dogrose”) + злово́нный (zlovónnyj, “fetid, foul-smelling”), a calque of translingual Rosa foetida.
шпа́га (špága, “type of sword”) + -ник (-nik, diminutive), calque of translingual Gladiolus.
Calque of translingual Thysanura. By surface analysis, щети́на (ščetína, “bristle”) + хвост (xvost, “tail”) + -ка (-ka).

parole.significato: Any snake of the genus Eirenis, certain colubrid snakes found in the Old World.
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Eirenis. Likely from Ancient Greek εἰρήνη f (eirḗnē, “peace”, noun).
Borrowed from translingual Eclipta, from Latin eclīpta, from Ancient Greek ἐκλείπω (ekleípō, “to leave out, to pass over”).
Calque of translingual Eclipta prostrata. By surface analysis, экли́пта (eklípta, “eclipta”) + простёртый (prostjórtyj, “prostrated”).

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Endocellion.
A plant of the genus Ensete.
Any member of the genus Epipremnum of climbing vines.
Any plant of the genus Echinodorus.
Any longhorn beetle of the genus Judolia.
